title: W9 counters span the full 3000-tick run while the envelope (MIN_LAND and per-host bound) is window-sized — effective landing tolerance ~0.89 not 0.95, and the per-host bound can false-fail a legal at-cap host
detail: The counting loop starts at tick 1, not SURGE_START=1200, and has no window filter: ~1200 pre-window base spawns (1/tick × 1200 ticks) inflate stream_spawned, lowering the 0.95×18000 landing floor to ~0.88×18000. The per-host bound (host: 2 + 1333×1800/1000 = 2401) is checked against a 3000-tick count — a host legally at cap all run (~4000 spawns) would false-fail credit_ok; it passes on seed 4243 only because growth spreads the load.
recommended_fix: Count only ticks in [SURGE_START, SURGE_END): guard the accumulation with `if tick >= SURGE_START` (or compute the bound with the full run length). Keeps the 0.95 tolerance and the cap×window+burst envelope exact.

title: cap_fraction_permille in [1,5] truncates residential accrual to 0 milli — the type becomes permanently spawn-ineligible and residential-sourced demand silently dies inside the validated 1..1000 range
detail: For residential (throughput 5, packet_bandwidth 30), any legal permille ≤ 5 gives floor(permille×5/30) = 0 milli/tick: credit never reaches SPAWN_CREDIT_ELIGIBLE 1000, so residential terminals are never pickable — email demand lands zero with no error. The adjacent comment rejects permille 0 exactly to avoid silent disable, but integer truncation recreates it at the range's low edge.
recommended_fix: At catalog load, fail-fast when spawn_credit_accrue_milli(cat, type) == 0 for any terminal type (or floor the accrual at 1 milli per live terminal), keeping the low-permille edge from silently starving a sourcing type.
